questions.questionHTML: According to the passage, why is retail CBDC (e₹-R) fundamentally different from decentralized cryptocurrencies?
questions.passageHTML:
Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) & The Future of Retail Payments

The Reserve Bank of India’s introduction of the Digital Rupee (e₹) marks a paradigm shift in the sovereign monetary architecture. Unlike decentralized cryptocurrencies, which suffer from inherent volatility and lack sovereign backing, CBDCs represent legal tender in a digital form issued directly by the central bank. Retail CBDC (e₹-R) offers an electronic counterpart to physical cash, aiming to preserve the direct public access to sovereign money while optimizing cash handling logistics.

A critical technical frontier in CBDC design is the delicate equilibrium between transactional privacy and regulatory compliance. Complete anonymity risks facilitating illicit financial flows, whereas total surveillance undermines public trust. The RBI has adopted a tier-based architecture where low-value transactions retain near-cash privacy, while high-value settlements mandate Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (CFT) verifications. Interoperability with the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) QR code ecosystem has significantly catalyzed merchant acceptance, allowing consumers to scan standard merchant QR codes and transact directly from their CBDC wallets without requiring merchants to install proprietary terminals.

Moreover, the programmability aspect of CBDCs opens unprecedented avenues for targeted social subsidies, agricultural input financing, and cross-border remittances. By enabling money to be earmarked for specific geographic regions or expenditure types (such as fertilizer subsidies or educational tuition), CBDC significantly curtails leakage and systemic slippage inherent in traditional fiscal disbursements.

Question 39: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively, while waste pipe C can empty it in 15 minutes. If all three pipes are opened together, in how many minutes will the cistern be completely filled?
questions.explanationHTML: Net work per minute = 1/20 + 1/30 - 1/15 = (3 + 2 - 4) / 60 = 1/60. Hence, cistern fills in 60 minutes.

questions.questionHTML: Question 40: A boat travels 36 km downstream in 3 hours and takes 6 hours to return the same distance upstream. What is the speed of the current?
questions.explanationHTML:
Downstream speed = 36/3 = 12 km/h. Upstream speed = 36/6 = 6 km/h.
Speed of current = (12 - 6) / 2 = 3 km/h.

questions.questionHTML: Question 55: A boat travels 36 km downstream in 3 hours and takes 6 hours to return the same distance upstream. What is the speed of the current?
questions.explanationHTML:
Downstream speed = 36/3 = 12 km/h. Upstream speed = 36/6 = 6 km/h.
Speed of current = (12 - 6) / 2 = 3 km/h.
